title: Learning fast by building small
excerpt: Tighter feedback loops beat big plans. Small, frequent builds help you learn faster and ship with confidence.
contentHtml:
Small projects compound. Each one trains your taste, improves your tools, and adds a reusable snippet to your personal library. When you build small, you can finish, reflect, and iterate. That loop is where speed comes from.

Pick a problem that fits in a weekend. Define a single user outcome. Cut scope until you can demo it in thirty seconds. Then ship. Capture notes while the context is fresh, and immediately plan the next tiny upgrade.

Momentum creates clarity. If it feels slow, reduce scope again. Your only goal is to keep the loop alive.
